svg.title: Atmospheric Effect Stack Order
svg.desc: The recommended order for stacking post-processing effects, shown as a vertical pipeline. From first to last: Glare and bloom to spread light from bright areas, then lens effects like chromatic aberration and distortion, then film grain for texture, then a final sharpen pass. Each stage explains why it sits where it does. Order matters because effects applied out of sequence compound incorrectly, for example sharpening before grain amplifies noise.
svg.text: Stack effects in the right order
Out of order, effects compound wrong — sharpening before grain amplifies noise; grain before bloom gets washed out.
Spread light from bright pixels first, while the image is still clean — blooms should read as light, not amplified grain.
Chromatic aberration, distortion, vignette — simulate the lens the light passed through, applied to the bloomed image.
Add texture over the graded, lensed image — grain sits on top of the "film," not underneath the optical effects.
Final crispening for delivery — do it last so it isn't blurred by later steps, and keep it subtle to avoid haloing.
